sourceFacts.fact: Impaired bile flow reduces bilirubin-derived pigment reaching stool.
Conjugated bilirubin can accumulate in blood and be excreted in urine.

labels: Cholestasis changes stool and urine colour
layout: A branching concept diagram. Node1 at top centre. LEFT branch node2 then node3 downward, ending with an ivory colour swatch labelled Pale stool; no stool sculpture. RIGHT branch node4 then node5 then node6 downward, ending with a dark amber droplet token labelled Dark urine. Draw arrows only between the named connected nodes. Keep the two branches separate and the bottom endpoints aligned. A small note under node4 reads: Water-soluble. No organs or tubes.

requiredChecks: Left branch means less pigment in stool, right branch means bilirubin in urine
No kidney, liver, ducts or urinary tract
No gallstone or specific cause of cholestasis is depicted
